author: Shreyas Gupta
complements: Ionic_Portfolio_Review (the deep reference for the scoring chain itself)
changes: references/08_do_not_regress.md gains three sections from the 170-ask audit: the seven claims the deck made about itself and could not support, why a tier that does not change the deck is not a tier, and why the documented command must be tested on the fixture shipped beside it.

CORRECTION, and the most consequential one in this skill: the fund-Sell rule as written in v1.4-v1.8 ("both frameworks independently at Sell") CAN NEVER FIRE - the long-term framework has no Sell verdict at all. The ruled and implemented rule is ORIGINATE-AND-VETO: the short-term capture framework originates, the long-term one vetoes on a CALIBRE A or B grade and raises a contradiction that must reach a human. The deck kit uses a THIRD path, the exporter's percentile rule, and the two can disagree on the same fund; the manual now says so instead of asserting a test nobody can apply.
The Sell backtest is stated honestly: 906 formations, buy leg hits 66%, sell leg hits 49.3%. Never present a fund Sell as backtested.
Tier table replaced with measured page counts and the reason they vary (book size, not tier).

The delivery branch is demo/deck-kit, which is where this skill actually is. It declared master and was never on it, so check_version returned unknown for every recipient. Merging to master is a separate decision and this line changes in the same commit as that merge, never before it.

check_version.py --update now fetches references/*.md as well as SKILL.md and VERSION.json. It copied only the two, so a recipient who updated got a current front page pointing at nine reference files they did not have. The list comes from reference_files in this manifest, so a future release can add a tenth without editing the script.

check_sync.py now fails on the SCORING METHOD being tracked in the public repo, not just the score files. Twelve such files were tracked and pushed; the gate listed only the kit's own filenames, which is why it never fired.

slidekit.fmt_score: one formatter, and a score of 0 reads "<1". A printed 0 reads as missing data and the desk forbids it; 0 is not missing (the fund score is the share of its own peer group a scheme beat, so 0 means it beat none) and blanking it would hide 52 rows, every one a Sell.
build_client_workbook.py prices a Trim on the trimmed SLICE. Priced on the full position, an over-cap holding's tax read several times the real bill.

allocation_house_view is no longer force-enabled by the kit. engine.py retired it on 2026-08-06 by Principal order ("confirm delete, not just hide") and a tier override was resurrecting it into finished client decks.

totals.mf_pct counts schemes only. It was struck on the pre-split frame, which still holds the direct shares, so the snapshot page told a client 67% of the book was held through funds where 46% is - the other 21 points being 124 directly held shares.

Wired three things that existed and were never called: check_method.py (on the live ctx), lib/mf_sell_gates.py (the Layer-1 vetoes and the churn arithmetic, which left fund_churn as {} on every build), and the profile argument to the risk/liquidity band loader, which now refuses to pass the Aggressive sheet off as a Moderate client's silently.

run_review.py fails the run on a module that produced NO page, ahead of any geometry finding: a geometry finding is a page laid out badly, a module that raised is a page the client will never see, and the deck around it looks finished.
references/08_do_not_regress.md: the consumer-with-no-producer pattern, the .get(k, 0) trap against a present-but-None value, and the shadowed-import trap between lib/ and modules/.

modules/return_arithmetic.py: what a client's stated return ambition requires of the money that can actually move, once the part held in another member's name or locked into a product is set aside. Renders nothing without --target-return. Not a Buy and names no product; where the required rate passes 20% it says the number is not one this desk will present as achievable.

references/09_subskills.md states the line this product does not cross: a proposed model portfolio with named products is a Buy, and the redeployment modules were cut permanently. Reversing a permanent cut is the Principal's call, not a build decision.

modules/family_implementation.py: who holds what, and who the plan lands on. The statement's holder column was thrown away at the parse, so no page could say that this family's debt sale fell 35% on the member holding 24% of the money. Renders nothing on a single-holder book.

references/09_subskills.md: the six other skills that touch this product, folded in. Carries the dual-framework fund Sell rule, the short-term method's four rulings and its material workbook bug, the look-through debt flags and tax-inertia rule, the mechanical layer's thresholds (asymmetric override bars, context-aware balance-sheet gate, commodity-cycle lens, single-group concentration at 20%, sector 20-25%, liquidity over 10 days, clutter under 0.25%), and the transfer-in floor of Rs 1 Cr per member and Rs 2.5 Cr per family.

SKILL.md surfaces one discrepancy rather than resolving it: the published fund Sell is struck on one framework's two horizons, and the desk's rule needs two frameworks. That is a method question for the desk; the manual says to check both or get FM sign-off before a fund Sell goes out.

run_review.py builds the CLIENT workbook too. Left as a separate command it was a step somebody forgets, and forgetting it attaches the raw reconciliation frame - raw field headings, and rationale text naming the firm own model - to a client email.
SKILL.md names the two workbooks apart: <Client>_Portfolio_Workbook.xlsx goes out, <Client>_Holdings.xlsx reconciles and does not.

Capture ratios: export_score_file.py now publishes up_capture / down_capture / capture_months / capture_ref, computed from the same monthly NAV panel as the score against the scheme own SEBI-category peer average. Four modules had read those fields since the kit was written and got None on every build, so the equity fund page skipped its capture panel and the per-scheme scorecards printed a dash.

qa/check_sync.py warns on a STARVED column - one the deck reads and the published file does not carry. A self-gating page renders nothing, which on a finished deck is indistinguishable from a page the desk chose not to include.

run_review.py: one command for build + graft + all three gates, exiting non-zero on any finding that lands on a generated page and writing out/<Client>_RUN.json so a deck can be traced back to its inputs and score-file dates.
qa/check_sync.py: one command that says whether the score files, the band files, the concentration cap, the skill and the git tree actually agree. Run it before any client build.
One skill for the whole review pipeline: statement in, deck and reconciling workbook out.
Documents the ionic-deck-kit path (statement -> build_review.py) as primary; the hand-written pr_template ctx path is the legacy route.
references/03_client_directives.md: the overlay that records a client's own instructions without the firm's name landing on calls it never made.
references/04_tax.md: the lot-aware tax engine - LTCG / STCG / post-Apr-2023 slices, equity STCG at 20%, slab money disclosed and never estimated.
references/08_do_not_regress.md: every defect this deck has shipped once, each of which passed all three QA gates.

Corrects the repo-visibility claim: shreyas1gupta-wq/ionic-scorecard is PUBLIC (verified 2026-09-08 via the GitHub API). Score files, band files, VERSION.json and every client artefact are gitignored and must stay that way.
notes: sequence is the field compared for staleness; version is for humans.
